title: How marketers are measuring AI search
gist: Marketing leaders at Cloudinary, Wix and other portfolio companies report that Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) attribution is structurally unmeasurable — AI assistants do not pass referral data and buying decisions now complete before the click — so first movers are replacing single-metric attribution with proxy stacks (AI visibility score via Profound, shuffled self-reported surveys, GA4 AI-referral traffic, behavioral anomalies, branded search volume). The counterintuitive operating signal is that non-branded traffic is falling while conversion per user rises double digits and GEO-sourced pipeline conversion runs up to 3x channel average, meaning traffic-volume defense with paid spend is the wrong response.

insights.claim: When buyers research a category inside an AI assistant, they arrive at a vendor's site with the decision largely already made, so last-click attribution credits the confirmation rather than the conversion and systematically undercounts Generative Engine Optimization's contribution.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Any SaaS company still budgeting channels off last-click dashboards is misallocating spend away from the channel actually creating demand — watch for CMOs who reprice GEO investment upward as this reframe spreads.
insights.quote: The click you’re crediting could be the confirmation, not the conversion.
insights.locator: The pre-click problem

insights.claim: AI assistants do not pass referral data the same way traditional search touchpoints did, which makes a single clean metric for AI-sourced demand technically unavailable rather than merely unbuilt.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: The measurement gap is structural, not a tooling lag — creates durable demand for AI-visibility analytics vendors rather than a temporary one.
insights.locator: Stop waiting for perfect GEO attribution

insights.claim: Vendors claiming to have solved AI search attribution should be treated as sales pitches, because no complete GEO attribution system currently exists.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Useful diligence filter when underwriting martech and AI-visibility startups pitching 'full-funnel AI attribution' — the practitioner consensus is that the claim is not credible.
insights.quote: “Whoever says they have it perfectly set up is probably trying to sell something,” she shared. “It doesn’t really exist right now.”
insights.locator: Stop waiting for perfect GEO attribution

insights.claim: Last-click attribution was never an accurate model of how purchase decisions were made — it was simply the most measurable proxy available — so AI search exposes a pre-existing fiction rather than creating a new problem.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Reframes the whole marketing-analytics stack as convention rather than ground truth; supports vendors selling incrementality and modeled attribution over deterministic click tracking.
insights.quote: “Decisions now start to happen before the click,” says Paula.
insights.locator: Last click was always a convention

insights.claim: Cloudinary's growth marketing team abandoned the search for a single AI-search metric and instead built a system of three proxies — AI visibility score, self-reported attribution, and AI chatbot referral traffic — that together produce enough signal to make decisions.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A replicable template for portfolio companies; the three-proxy pattern is likely to become the de facto standard measurement stack for AI search.
insights.locator: Stop waiting for perfect GEO attribution

insights.claim: Cloudinary targets a 75% overall share of voice on its tracked keyword prompt groups in Profound, tracking AI visibility top-down through Profound and bottom-up through Google Search Console.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: First concrete public benchmark for what a sophisticated team sets as an AI share-of-voice target — a yardstick for evaluating any company's GEO position.
insights.locator: Her first proxy is an AI visibility score

insights.claim: Cloudinary holds a 91% AI visibility score on the question 'What's a reliable image API for automatic pre-processing?', an outcome attributed to years of developer adoption and embedded-product growth rather than to any GEO campaign.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Suggests incumbency and genuine category embeddedness — not optimization spend — is the main driver of AI answer share, which favors established product-led companies over new entrants trying to buy visibility.
insights.locator: Her first proxy is an AI visibility score

insights.claim: Self-reported attribution surveys should periodically shuffle their response options so that the AI referral choice sometimes appears first, avoiding anchoring bias, and should be validity-checked by split-testing the question across two audience cohorts to look for consistency.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Operational detail that determines whether 'how did you hear about us' data is usable; inconsistency across cohorts is the tell that collection or interpretation is broken.
insights.locator: The second proxy is self-reported attribution

insights.claim: Tracking ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude as identifiable GA4 sources — now also surfaced under an 'AI Assistant' grouping — is the most familiar but most incomplete measurement surface, because it captures only users who clicked from an AI interface and misses the larger group influenced by an AI answer who arrive through another path.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Explains why headline 'AI referral traffic is only ~1% of sessions' stats badly understate AI's commercial influence — do not size the AI search opportunity off GA4 referral counts.
insights.locator: Her third proxy is referral traffic from AI chatbots

themes.theme: Traffic down, conversion up: the inverted funnel

insights.claim: At Wix, non-branded organic traffic fell while average conversion per user grew by double digits year over year, indicating AI-driven traffic is smaller in volume but composed of stronger prospects.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Declining organic traffic at consumer and SMB software companies may be a mix-shift signal rather than a demand deterioration signal — check conversion per user before marking down a business on traffic decay.
insights.locator: The traffic paradox

insights.claim: One marketing team reported that conversion to pipeline from GEO-sourced leads ran at triple their channel average, described by that CMO as an unprecedented channel-level pipeline lift.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: If 3x channel-average pipeline conversion generalizes, GEO is currently the highest-ROI acquisition channel in B2B software and is materially underfunded relative to paid search.
insights.quote: “I’ve never in my career seen a channel increase pipeline 3x,” that CMO shared.
insights.locator: Less traffic can mean better business outcomes

insights.claim: The structural explanation for higher-quality AI-sourced traffic is that the funnel has narrowed at the top and become more efficient in the middle: buyers evaluate options and form a preference inside the AI conversation before ever visiting a vendor site.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Implies middle-of-funnel nurture content and MQL-stage tooling lose value while brand-level presence in model answers gains it — a negative second-order read for volume-based lead-gen and content-farm businesses.
insights.locator: The explanation is a structural one

insights.claim: Reaching for paid media to prop up falling organic traffic volume risks buying a dashboard number rather than incremental conversion, and the more useful CMO question is what the actual relationship is between organic and paid spend.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Watch for a wave of paid-search budget reallocation as CMOs test incrementality — a potential headwind to search-ad revenue growth that is separate from AI answer cannibalization.
insights.locator: Paula flags the risk of teams

themes.theme: Branded search and the language-layer gap

insights.claim: Branded search volume is a more resilient indicator of demand creation than non-branded traffic, because people searching a brand name prove demand is being generated upstream — through AI recommendations, editorial coverage or community mentions — even when the source cannot be traced.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Branded search volume becomes the durable KPI to monitor for any consumer or SMB software name in an AI-answer world; it is the 'footprint of influence that doesn't require a click'.
insights.locator: A more resilient indicator

insights.claim: Content volume has stopped being the default growth lever, with organic growth teams shifting from producing large quantities of content to asking whether each piece is worth creating at all.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Structurally bearish for volume content production, freelance content supply chains and SEO content tooling priced per article; bullish for brand and messaging consistency tooling.
insights.quote: “I now ask myself: Is all content worth creating? The answer is no. Saying yes to something comes at the cost of saying no to something else.”
insights.locator: Our organic growth teams used to spend

insights.claim: The emerging optimization target is a brand's 'language layer' gap: rather than pushing more content, teams align all communications around a common language and ensure third-party language reflects the same messaging.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A new category of marketing work — messaging consistency enforcement across owned and third-party surfaces — that currently has no dominant tooling vendor.
insights.locator: The goal now is to address

insights.claim: Educational content that once drove measurable traffic may still be shaping purchase decisions invisibly inside AI conversations, meaning a resource can influence a buyer and never appear anywhere in the vendor's analytics.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Cutting content that shows zero attributed traffic may destroy demand generation that is still working — a live risk of over-pruning content budgets on bad data.
insights.quote: “Educational content that used to drive traffic may still be shaping decisions—we just can't see it anymore.”
insights.locator: Last click was always a convention

themes.theme: GEO as a company-wide mandate, not a marketing project

insights.claim: SEO could be owned and siloed by a single team because that team controlled most inputs and outputs, whereas GEO spans content, PR, community, social and even employee-generated content and therefore cannot be contained in one function.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Organizational design, not tooling, is the binding constraint on GEO performance — a diligence question for any company claiming AI search readiness.
insights.locator: GEO requires company-wide buy-in

insights.claim: Wix enforces 'semantic triples' — a common vocabulary used by every team producing assets, so that an SEO page, a community post and a journalist briefing all describe Wix products with identical specific language, reinforcing the same brand-topic associations in the models.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Concrete, copyable mechanism for influencing model associations; the emphasis on entity-relationship consistency hints at how model training and retrieval reward vocabulary repetition.
insights.locator: At Wix, this meant establishing

insights.claim: PR has become the biggest single unlock for GEO at Wix — where PR sits outside marketing — because journalists are now briefed with the same controlled vocabulary before every major story, making vocabulary-aligned press an operational requirement rather than a brand nicety.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Re-rates earned media and PR agency value in an AI-search world; third-party publication is now a direct input to model visibility rather than a soft awareness play.
insights.quote: “If it gets published, it helps,” Paula says. “It's become almost an operational requirement for GEO to be effective.”
insights.locator: The biggest unlock from this approach

insights.claim: Cloudinary structures GEO as a flywheel split between branded and non-branded motions with distinct owners at each funnel stage, and its newest motion is 'AX' or agentic experience — designing content and product surfaces for AI agents making decisions on behalf of users.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Early signal that the next optimization surface is agent-readable product and docs, which matters most for API and infrastructure vendors whose buyers will be agents first.
insights.quote: “That's critical for infrastructure companies,” she says.
insights.locator: At Cloudinary, Natalia says

insights.claim: At one vertical AI company every marketing meeting opens with ten minutes of 'who's done something new with AI?' and an entire company offsite was dedicated to GEO, with the mandate framed as needing to come from the CEO down.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Cultural ritual as an adoption mechanism; CEO-level sponsorship is the observable marker separating companies making GEO progress from those running it as a side project.
insights.quote: “It has to be non-negotiable. This is such a transformational moment.”
insights.locator: A CMO at a vertical AI company

insights.claim: The teams systematically underestimating GEO's contribution are precisely the ones waiting for clean attribution before committing budget, while the teams gaining advantage started measuring imperfectly and moved anyway.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Creates a measurable dispersion between early and late GEO adopters that should show up in organic pipeline efficiency over the next several quarters.
insights.locator: Start measuring AI imperfectly now

insights.claim: One vertical AI CMO deliberately applies an upward correction to self-reported survey data when response rates are low enough to undercount meaningfully, and tags behavioral anomalies as GEO on heuristics, explicitly rejecting methodological purity as the validation standard.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Shows practitioners intentionally biasing estimates upward to counter known undercounting — reported GEO contribution figures across the industry will be noisy and non-comparable.
insights.quote: “We’re systematically underestimating what we're allocating to GEO,” they say.
insights.locator: The vertical AI CMO adds a tax

insights.claim: A weekly review cycle covering visibility score, sentiment and truth score, and recommendation position has replaced quarterly reporting cadence for AI search, on the argument that the channel now moves too fast for quarterly reviews.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: Weekly cadence plus three named metrics defines the emerging AI-search reporting standard; vendors that can deliver these three metrics weekly have a clear product wedge.
insights.quote: “Things move too fast now for quarterly reviews,” says the CMO.
insights.locator: Their team also runs a weekly review cycle

insights.claim: Cloudinary runs 120–150 experiments per quarter and is scaling that program up for GEO, treating each manipulation for AI as a discrete experiment.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A concrete experimentation-velocity benchmark; companies running an order of magnitude fewer tests are unlikely to keep pace in a channel where the rules change monthly.
insights.locator: Natalia says they run 120–150 experiments

insights.claim: Recency keywords such as 'best XYZ in 2026' trigger a live search in models because every model has a knowledge cutoff, and content optimized with these keywords can surface in AI answers within 2-4 weeks.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: The single fastest-acting GEO tactic disclosed here, with a stated 2-4 week payback — an immediately testable lever for any portfolio company losing organic visibility.
insights.quote: “Every model has a knowledge cutoff, and recency keywords—like ‘best XYZ in 2026’—trigger a live search for the latest information. This is a fast win when you're trying to be visible within a week or two on specific queries.”
insights.locator: One experiment they conduct is the use of recency keywords

insights.claim: A vertical software CMO inverts the measurement approach by reading anomalies already present in analytics rather than building new tracking: when an 'unknown' traffic source spiked in one quarter, the team attributed it to AI and tracked it as GEO, on the logic that a deep, previously untrafficked product page has only one plausible discovery route.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A zero-cost measurement method requiring no new tooling — reclassifying 'unknown/direct' traffic is likely the fastest way most companies can start quantifying AI-sourced demand.
insights.quote: “Would I say it’s a 100% science? Absolutely not. But that’s the nature of the beast right now.”
insights.locator: A vertical software CMO approached the same problem

insights.claim: A recommended starter AI measurement system pairs six KPIs with explicit methods: AI visibility score via Profound, AI referral traffic via GA4 source/medium, behavioral anomalies via deep product page spikes and reclassified 'unknown' traffic, self-reported attribution with shuffled options and a 3x correction when responses are low, branded search volume via Google Search Console, and pipeline conversion rate benchmarked against channel average.
insights.speaker: Taj Shorter
insights.so_what: A ready-made scorecard to run against any portfolio company's marketing org to assess whether it is instrumented for AI search at all.
insights.locator: Build your own GEO measurement stack
